heard: Black holes usually kill stars, but this one births them. Discovered in 2010, the Phoenix cluster lies in the southern constellation of Phoenix. The cluster creates new stars at a rate of more than 700 per year. In comparison, the Milky Way forms roughly one or two stars per year. NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory detected giant holes in the surrounding hot gas. Hubble revealed filaments of cooler gas where new stars form. Its 10 billion solar mass black hole fails to act as a normal thermostat. This growth spurt cannot last longer than a hundred million years. That is why black holes usually kill stars, but this one births them.
